title: A2 Writing Quiz 6 — Food, Restaurants & City Life

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you ever tried sushi before?
Have you ever try sushi before?
Did you ever tried sushi before?
Have you ever tries sushi before?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Have + subject + past participle: 'Have you ever tried sushi before?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have eaten at that restaurant last week.
We ate at that restaurant last week.
We have eat at that restaurant last week.
We are eating at that restaurant last week.
questions.explanation: A specific past time ('last week') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was ordering food when my friend called.
I ordered food when my friend was calling.
I was order food when my friend called.
I ordering was food when my friend called.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'I was ordering food when my friend called.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This café is quieter than the one downtown.
This café is more quiet than the one downtown.
This café is quietest than the one downtown.
This café is quiet than the one downtown.
questions.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y often take -er: 'quieter than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the most delicious meal I've ever had.
This is the more delicious meal I've ever had.
This is deliciousest meal I've ever had.
This is delicious meal I've ever had.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'the most' for superlatives: 'the most delicious meal'.

questions.topic: Modal verbs (can I / could I for requests)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Could I have the menu, please?
Could I to have the menu, please?
Could I having the menu, please?
I could have the menu, please?
questions.explanation: 'Could' is followed by the base form of the verb in polite requests: 'Could I have...?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have to book a table in advance on weekends.
We has to book a table in advance on weekends.
We have to booking a table in advance on weekends.
We have to booked a table in advance on weekends.
questions.explanation: 'Have to' + base verb expresses necessity: 'have to book'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You should try the local dishes here.
You should to try the local dishes here.
You should trying the local dishes here.
You should tries the local dishes here.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'should try'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We're going to eat out tonight.
We're going eat out tonight.
We going to eat out tonight.
We're going to eating out tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to eat out'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the restaurant is full, we will wait outside.
If the restaurant will be full, we wait outside.
If the restaurant is full, we wait will outside.
If the restaurant was full, we will wait outside.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If the restaurant is full, we will wait outside.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I don't feel like cooking tonight.
I don't feel like to cook tonight.
I don't feel like cook tonight.
I don't feel like cooked tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Feel like' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'feel like cooking'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We agreed splitting the bill equally.
We agreed to split the bill equally.
We agreed split the bill equally.
We agreed for split the bill equally.
questions.explanation: 'Agree' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'agreed to split'.

questions.question: There aren't ___ vegetarian options on this menu.
options: much
many
a little
much of
questions.explanation: 'Options' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used in negative sentences.

questions.question: Could you add ___ salt to the soup, please?
options: a few
a little
many
few
questions.explanation: 'Salt' is uncountable, and 'a little' means 'a small amount of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'as well as'.
options: The café serves coffee as well as fresh pastries.
The café serves coffee as well fresh pastries.
As well as the café serves coffee and pastries.
The café serves coffee, as well as, fresh pastries.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' connects two items and means 'in addition to': 'coffee as well as fresh pastries.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I ordered soup instead of salad.
I ordered soup instead salad.
I ordered soup instead of eat salad.
I ordered soup instead of salad but.
questions.explanation: 'Instead of' is followed by a noun: 'soup instead of salad.'

questions.question: The new bakery is ___ the bus station.
options: next to
next of
nearby to
close from
questions.explanation: 'Next to' + noun describes a position: 'next to the bus station.'

questions.question: There are many good restaurants ___ this area.
options: around
along
across
besides
questions.explanation: 'Around' can mean 'in the surrounding area': 'restaurants around this area.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I love this restaurant.")
options: She said that she loves this restaurant.
She said that she loved that restaurant.
She said that she is loving this restaurant.
She said she love that restaurant.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple shifts to past simple, and 'this' often shifts to 'that': 'she loved that restaurant.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a restaurant to book a table?
options: Hey guys,
Dear Sir/Madam,
Yo,
Hiya,
questions.explanation: 'Dear Sir/Madam,' is used when writing formally to a business without knowing the recipient's name.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a formal email requesting a reservation?
options: Yours faithfully,
Catch you later,
Cheers,
Take care,
questions.explanation: 'Yours faithfully,' matches 'Dear Sir/Madam,' when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Why don't we try the new noodle place downtown?
Why we don't try the new noodle place downtown?
Why not we try the new noodle place downtown?
Why don't we trying the new noodle place downtown?
questions.explanation: 'Why don't we' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Why don't we try...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the restaurant.' and 'We had our first date there.'?
options: This is the restaurant who we had our first date.
This is the restaurant where we had our first date.
This is the restaurant which we had our first date.
This is the restaurant what we had our first date.
questions.explanation: 'Where' is used for places in relative clauses: 'the restaurant where we had our first date.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We often eat out on Fridays.
We eat often out on Fridays.
Often we eat out on Fridays always.
We eat out often on Fridays.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'We often eat out.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Could you tell me if this dish is spicy?
Could you tell me is this dish spicy?
Could you tell me if this dish is spicy.
Could you tell me, if this dish is spicy?
questions.explanation: Indirect yes/no questions use 'if' with normal word order and end with a question mark.

questions.question: The chef ___ all day, so dinner should be amazing.
options: cooks
has cooked
has been cooking
cooked
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action explaining a present result: 'has been cooking'.

questions.question: This dessert isn't mine, it's ___.
options: she
her
hers
her's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's hers.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, order drinks. Next, choose a starter. Finally, pick the main course.
First order drinks next choose starter finally pick main course.
Finally order drinks, first choose starter, next pick main course.
Next first order drinks, finally choose pick main course.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Next,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every table in the restaurant ___ a small candle.
options: have
has
having
are having
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every table has...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: This soup is delicious, isn't it?
This soup is delicious, is it?
This soup is delicious, doesn't it?
This soup is delicious, isn't?
questions.explanation: Positive statement + negative tag: 'This soup is delicious, isn't it?'
